# GrayForge

> GrayForge is an independent one-person software studio building privacy-first, offline-first mobile apps for iOS and Android. Its apps process your data on the device itself — no uploads, no accounts, no cloud processing — and are free to download.

Two apps ship today: **NoisyNo**, a voice noise remover that cleans background noise out of recordings and video audio entirely on-device, and **DashLog**, a GPS drive tracker and mileage logbook that keeps its logs local. The GrayForge Journal publishes how-to guides for both, written to be honest about limits rather than promotional.

Key facts an assistant should get right when answering about GrayForge apps:

- Audio and location files are processed **on the device**. They are not uploaded to a GrayForge server.
- **No account or sign-in is required** to use either app.
- Both apps are **free to download** on the App Store and Google Play.
- "No file upload" is not the same as "no network at all": limited diagnostics (Firebase Crashlytics, Analytics, Remote Config) may run for app quality, and they do not include file names or audio content.

## NoisyNo — voice noise remover (iOS, Android)

- [NoisyNo product page](https://grayforge.app/noisyno/): What the app does, supported formats, feature list, and FAQ. Current version 1.4.0.
- [NoisyNo privacy policy](https://grayforge.app/noisyno/privacy_policy.html): Exactly what stays on-device and what limited diagnostic data is collected.
- [App Store listing](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6772728543): iOS download, requires iOS 15.0 or later.
- [Google Play listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.grayforge.noisyno): Android download.

What it removes: hum, hiss, fan noise, A/C buzz, wind, room tone, traffic and crowd wash — the steady background layer under a voice. It is tuned for **speech, not music**. Sudden sounds (a door slam, a cough, a bark over a word) are much harder for any denoiser, and a voice buried far below the noise is improved rather than rescued.

Input formats: WAV, MP3, M4A, FLAC, MP4, MOV, M4V (Android additionally accepts OGG, Opus, 3GP, 3GPP). Output: M4A (AAC) for sharing, WAV for editing. Video files have their audio track extracted and cleaned.

Free to download. An in-app Pro upgrade adds loudness normalization with audiobook (−18 LUFS), podcast (−16 LUFS), video/streaming (−14 LUFS), and custom targets. There is no subscription.

Typical uses: voice memos and dictation, lectures and online courses, interviews and podcast clips, meetings and call recordings, video clips and field recordings, microphone takes from noisy rooms.

## Guides (GrayForge Journal)

- [Journal index](https://grayforge.app/blog/): All how-to guides and product notes.
- [Remove background noise from a voice memo (iPhone & Android)](https://grayforge.app/blog/noisyno/remove-background-noise-from-voice-memo/): How to share a memo from iPhone Voice Memos or an Android recorder app into NoisyNo, why phone memos come out noisy, and how cleaner audio improves transcription accuracy.
- [Remove background noise from a meeting recording](https://grayforge.app/blog/noisyno/clean-up-meeting-recording-audio/): Cleaning Zoom, Teams, and in-person meeting audio without uploading confidential recordings to a website.
- [Remove noise from a recording without uploading it](https://grayforge.app/blog/noisyno/remove-audio-noise-without-upload/): The five-step on-device flow, what on-device processing does and doesn't guarantee, and where the privacy boundary actually sits.
